    Introduction

    <<<<<<< HEAD

    For domains \(D\subset \mathbb{R}^2\), the rSPDE package implements the anisotropic Matérn model \[ (I - \nabla\cdot (H\nabla))^{(\nu + 1)/2} u = c\sigma W, \quad \text{on } D \] Where \(H\) is a \(2\times 2\) positive definite matrix, \(\sigma, \nu >0\) and \(c\) is a constant chosen such that \(u\) would have the covariance function \[ r(h) = \frac{\sigma^2}{2^{\nu-1}\Gamma(\nu)} (\sqrt{h^T H^{-1} h})^{\nu} K_{\nu}(\sqrt{h^T H^{-1} h}), \] if the domain was \(D = \mathbb{R}^2\), i.e., a stationary and anisotropic Matérn covariance function.     Let us now simulate some data based on this simulated field.

    n.obs <- 2000
obs.loc <- cbind(runif(n.obs),runif(n.obs))

sigma.e <- 0.1
Y <- as.vector(A%*%u + sigma.e*rnorm(n.obs))

    Let us finally use rspde_lme to estimate the parameters based on the data.

    df <- data.frame(Y = as.matrix(Y), x = obs.loc[,1], y = obs.loc[,2])

    In the call, y~1 indicates that we also want to estimate a mean value of the model, and the arguments loc provides the names of the spatial and temporal coordinates in the data frame. Let us see a summary of the fitted model:
